title: Daily Market Digest
subtitle: As of Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Close, and Thursday, November 5, 2026 Pre-market

items.headline: Wall Street Surges on Democratic Midterm Sweep and Falling Oil Prices; Tech Diverges on AI Concerns
items.summary: U.S. equities closed sharply higher on Wednesday, driven by a broad-based rally as the Democratic sweep in the midterm elections eased political uncertainty and bolstered investor risk appetite. Plunging crude oil prices further fueled optimism. However, a notable divergence emerged within the technology sector, with AI-related stocks facing pressure amidst concerns over potential new regulations, which continued into Thursday's pre-market trading.

sections.title: Top Movers (Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Close / Thursday, November 5, 2026 Pre-market)

items.headline: Microsoft Rises on Broad Market Optimism
items.summary: Microsoft Corporation surged amidst the broader market rally, with investors anticipating benefits from potential shifts in AI investment dynamics.

items.headline: Amazon.com Jumps as Hyperscalers Gain
items.summary: Amazon.com, Inc. saw significant gains as hyperscaler stocks benefited from hopes of slower data center construction potentially cutting capital spending.

items.headline: Apple Hits All-Time High
items.summary: Apple Inc. reached a new all-time high, with investors hoping that slower data center construction will lead to lower memory prices, positively impacting Apple's margins.

items.headline: Trump Media & Technology Group Plummets Post-Midterms
items.summary: Trump Media & Technology Group experienced a sharp decline following the U.S. midterm election results, which may have shifted investor sentiment around its outlook.

items.headline: Qualcomm Slides on Weak Outlook
items.summary: Qualcomm shares fell significantly in pre-market trading on Thursday due to weak smartphone chip sales and a lower-than-expected EPS guidance for the next quarter.

items.headline: NVIDIA Declines Amid AI Sector Scrutiny
items.summary: NVIDIA Corp. saw declines as investors reassessed the implications of the midterm election for corporate regulation and potential restrictions on artificial intelligence development.

items.headline: Sector Rotation Underway: Consumer Discretionary, Financials Lead; Energy, Tech Lag
items.summary: Following the midterm elections, market sentiment shifted, leading to a rotation. Consumer Discretionary (+4.3%), Financials (+3.5%), and Real Estate (+3.2%) were among the leading sectors on Wednesday. Conversely, the Energy sector plunged 4.8% due to falling oil prices, and technology, particularly AI-related stocks, experienced selling pressure amid concerns about increased regulatory scrutiny.

items.headline: Key Economic Data: Trade Deficit Narrows, ISM Services Index Steady
items.summary: Recent economic data shows the U.S. trade deficit decreased to $105 billion in September, while the ISM Services Index for October registered 54.5, a slight dip from September's 54.9. U.S. commercial crude inventories also saw a decrease of 0.9 million barrels for the week ending October 30.

items.headline: Earnings Season Highlights: BCE, Southern Company, ConocoPhillips Report
items.summary: Several major companies released their Q3 2026 earnings. BCE Inc. reported 2.2% consolidated revenue growth but a 6.3% decrease in adjusted EPS. Southern Company announced strong Q3 earnings of $2.0 billion, up from $1.7 billion year-over-year. ConocoPhillips reported Q3 EPS of $3.34 and increased its quarterly dividend by 11%. Air Products saw a 12% rise in adjusted EPS for fiscal 2026.

items.headline: Oil Prices Plunge and Treasury Yields Fall Amid Hopes for Iran War Resolution
items.summary: Crude oil prices experienced a significant decline, with Brent crude falling 8.7% to $94.62 and WTI crude down 8.3% to $88.12, driven by optimism around a quicker end to the Iran war following the Democratic midterm victory. Concurrently, the yield on the benchmark U.S. 10-year Treasury note fell to 4.88%.
